uncited: Inverse CDF Ray Sampling generates sample points along a ray by mapping uniform random noise to depth intervals using the cumulative distribution function (CDF) derived from per-hit probabilities.

It solves the problem of stratified sampling within non-uniform depth bins defined by ray-triangle or ray-volume intersections, ensuring that samples are distributed according to the likelihood of each interval while maintaining stratification to reduce variance.

It differs from simple uniform sampling by weighting samples toward intervals with higher probability mass, and from pure stratified sampling by allowing arbitrary probability distributions rather than uniform bin weights.
